main_body: farm building (barn with pitched roof and front wall)
top_band: reddish-brown tiled roof slope with dormer, rows 6-57
evidence: The building clearly shows a large foreshortened roof slope from above (rows 6-57) with a distinct light yellow-tan front eave trim at rows 56-57, an eave shadow at rows 59-61, and the vertical south wall face below (rows 59-93) with inset windows and barn doors.

style.evidence: While the roof has a repetitive 4-step tile pattern, the lower wall and barn doors are much flatter and more geometric/clean than the Beodeul reference buildings. The red wood siding consists of uniform vertical stripes with large flat-filled areas, and the white door frames/crossbars and grey corner pillars are flat blocks of colour lacking the rich per-stone/per-plank grain, dithering, and organic shading variation of the references. The dormer roof also lacks tile texture.
